key_insight: A unified computational framework using control and game theory models co-adaptation between human users and decoders in closed-loop neural interfaces, enabling principled prediction and shaping of their joint dynamics to improve usability and personalization.
problem_solved: Unpredictable and poorly understood mutual adaptation between users and decoders in closed-loop brain–computer interfaces prevents reliable, personalized performance and makes decoder design ad hoc.
method: Formulate the user–decoder interaction as a coupled control / game-theoretic system of agents that adapt their policies to maximize task-related objectives.
Analyze equilibrium, stability, and transient dynamics to predict co-adaptive behavior and identify how decoder rules influence user learning.
Derive design principles and algorithmic prescriptions for decoder updates that steer the joint system toward desirable, personalized outcomes.
impact: Provides AI/ML practitioners with a principled toolkit to design and evaluate adaptive decoders for neural interfaces, improving reliability, convergence, and personalization of closed-loop systems.
visual_elements: Schematic of closed-loop system showing user and decoder as coupled agents with bidirectional feedback arrows.
Phase portrait or equilibrium diagram from game/control analysis illustrating stable vs unstable co-adaptive regimes.
Before/after usability chart comparing performance and convergence under standard vs theory-guided decoder designs.
Flowchart of design pipeline: model → stability analysis → decoder rule selection → experimental validation.
paper_title: Computational framework to predict and shape human–machine interactions in closed-loop, co-adaptive neural interfaces
paper_authors: Maneeshika M. Madduri, Momona Yamagami, Si Jia Li, Sasha Burckhardt, Samuel A. Burden
